title: How to motivate yourself and others, with Wendy Grolnick, PhD, and Frank Worrell, PhD

sentences.en: We all have things that we want to accomplish in life.
sentences.zh: 我们一生中都有想要完成的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe it's writing a book, or learning a new language, or running a 5K.
sentences.zh: 也许是写一本书，或者是学习一门新语言，又或是跑一次五公里。

sentences.en: Or maybe you want to motivate someone else in your life to do something tough, like getting your kids to improve their grades.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可能想激励生活中的某个人去做一些艰难的事，比如让你的孩子提高成绩。

sentences.en: But no matter how much you try to bribe, cajole, or inspire, you're just not seeing the changes you want, or making the changes in yourself.
sentences.zh: 但无论你如何努力去利诱、哄劝或鼓舞，你就是看不到自己想要的改变，或者在自己身上做出改变。

sentences.en: At that point, you might ask, why am I so unmotivated, or why are they so unmotivated?
sentences.zh: 在那时，你可能会问，为什么我这么缺乏动力，或者为什么他们这么缺乏动力？

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk to the authors of a new book on motivation myths, about what the science really says about motivation,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一本关于动机迷思的新书的作者们进行交谈，聊聊科学对动机的真实看法，

sentences.en: and about how our misconceptions get in the way of accomplishing our goals.
sentences.zh: 以及我们的误解是如何阻碍我们实现目标的。

sentences.en: We'll explore such questions as, do rewards work to motivate people?
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨诸如这样的问题：奖励真的能激发人们的动力吗？

sentences.en: Does competition inspire people to excel, or does it make them less motivated?
sentences.zh: 竞争能激励人们精益求精，还是会让他们失去动力？

sentences.en: What about praise?
sentences.zh: 那表扬呢？

sentences.en: Does praising people for their smarts or abilities help them to accomplish more?
sentences.zh: 因为聪明或能力而表扬人们，能帮助他们取得更多成就吗？

sentences.en: Are some people just basically unmotivated?
sentences.zh: 有些人是不是天生就缺乏动力？

sentences.en: Or is everyone motivated in the right context or situation?
sentences.zh: 还是说每个人在合适的环境或情境下都有动力？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Frank Worrell, a distinguished professor and director of the School Psychology Program at the University of California, Berkeley School of Education.
sentences.zh: 首先是弗兰克·沃雷尔博士，他是加利福尼亚大学伯克利分校教育学院学校心理学项目的杰出教授兼主任。

sentences.en: He also holds an affiliate appointment in the social and personality area in the Department of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 他还在心理学系的社会与人格领域担任兼职教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Worrell studies motivation in schools and educational settings.
sentences.zh: 沃雷尔博士主要研究学校和教育环境中的动机。

sentences.en: His areas of expertise include academic talent development and gifted education, at-risk youth, cultural identities, and teaching effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 他的专业领域包括学业人才开发与天才教育、弱势青年、文化认同以及教学效能。

sentences.en: He's author of more than 300 journal articles and book chapters, as well as five books, and he's won numerous awards for his research.
sentences.zh: 他是300多篇期刊文章和书籍章节的作者，也是五本书的作者，并因其研究获得过众多奖项。

sentences.en: He was also the 2022 president of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 他还是2022年美国心理学会的主席。

sentences.en: Also with us is Dr. Wendy Grolnick, a professor of psychology at Clark University.
sentences.zh: 与我们同行的还有克拉克大学心理学教授温迪·格罗尔尼克博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Grolnick is an expert on motivation and parenting.
sentences.zh: 格罗尔尼克博士是动机和育儿方面的专家。

sentences.en: She's conducted pioneering studies on the role that parents and teachers play in children's motivation and achievement.
sentences.zh: 她对父母和老师在儿童动机和成就中所起的作用进行了开创性的研究。

sentences.en: She has published more than 90 articles in scholarly journals, and her work has been funded by the National Institute of Mental Health, the William T.
sentences.zh: 她在学术期刊上发表了90多篇文章，她的研究得到了美国国家精神卫生研究所、威廉·T·

sentences.en: Grant Foundation, and the Spencer Foundation.
sentences.zh: 格兰特基金会和斯宾塞基金会的资助。

sentences.en: Drs.
sentences.zh: 沃雷尔博士

sentences.en: Worrell and Grolnick, together with Dr. Benjamin Hetty, are co-authors of the new book,
sentences.zh: 和格罗尔尼克博士与本杰明·赫蒂博士一起，是新书的合著者，

sentences.en: Motivation Mythbusters, Science-Based Strategies to Boost Motivation in Yourself and Others, to be published by APA Books in July.
sentences.zh: 该书名为《动机迷思终结者：激发自己和他人动机的科学策略》，将于7月由APA出版社出版。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 感谢两位今天能来参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Delighted to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Yeah, thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Let's start with the first myth you discuss in the book, which is the idea that some people are motivated while others just aren't.
sentences.zh: 让我们从你们书中讨论的第一个迷思开始，也就是那种认为有些人有动力而另一些人根本没有的观点。

sentences.en: I think a lot of us have the idea that motivation is some kind of a personality trait.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都认为动机是一种人格特质。

sentences.en: You either have it or you don't.
sentences.zh: 你要么有，要么没有。

sentences.en: Is that a myth?
sentences.zh: 这是一个迷思吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's a myth.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个迷思。

sentences.en: A lot of times we think of motivation as something about a person.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们认为动机是关于一个人本身的某种东西。

sentences.en: Some people are very motivated people.
sentences.zh: 有些人是非常有动力的人。

sentences.en: Other people are unmotivated people.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则是缺乏动力的人。

sentences.en: And it turns out what the science says is that motivation is really much more a function of people's interests and the context that they're in.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，科学告诉我们，动机实际上更多地取决于人们的兴趣以及他们所处的情境。

sentences.en: Everybody can be motivated in a particular context.
sentences.zh: 每个人在特定的情境下都可以是有动力的。

sentences.en: And there are some contexts that are more motivating than others.
sentences.zh: 而且有些情境比其他情境更能激发动力。

sentences.en: And I think the problem with holding the conception that some people are motivated and others aren't
sentences.zh: 我认为，持有“有些人有动力而另一些人没有”这种观念的问题在于，

sentences.en: is that if we see someone that doesn't look so motivated, we think that's a motivated person.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看到某人看起来没那么有动力，我们就会认为那是一个有动力的人。

sentences.en: We start to treat them as a motivated person, an unmotivated person.
sentences.zh: 我们开始把他们当作一个有动力的人，一个缺乏动力的人来对待。

sentences.en: And when we treat them as an unmotivated person, they might start to act like that more and fulfill that prophecy.
sentences.zh: 而当我们把他们当作一个缺乏动力的人来对待时，他们可能会开始表现得更像那样，并最终印证了这种预言。

sentences.en: So holding the idea that some people are motivated and others aren't can really get in the way of the way we treat other people.
sentences.zh: 因此，抱着“有些人有动力而另一些人没有”这种想法，真的会妨碍我们对待其他人的方式。

sentences.en: And if we start to see ourselves that way, can really get in the way of our reaching our goals.
sentences.zh: 如果我们开始这样看待自己，真的会阻碍我们实现目标。

sentences.en: Yes, I would add, if I could, that in speaking to parents and teachers, they are often saying, well, they're not motivated.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果可以的话我想补充一点，在与父母和老师交谈时，他们经常说，嗯，他们没有动力。

sentences.en: They seem so unmotivated.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来太缺乏动力了。

sentences.en: And I ask, well, what are they doing?
sentences.zh: 我问，那他们在做什么？

sentences.en: Are they not doing anything?
sentences.zh: 他们什么都不做吗？

sentences.en: Well, they're playing video games all day or they're reading.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们一整天都在玩电子游戏或者在读书。

sentences.en: So they're motivated to do something.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是有动力做某些事情的。

sentences.en: They're just not motivated to do what the parent or the teacher wants them to do.
sentences.zh: 他们只是对父母或老师想让他们做的事情没有动力。

sentences.en: If motivation isn't actually a personality trait, what is it?
sentences.zh: 如果动机实际上不是一种人格特质，那它是什么？

sentences.en: So motivation is a sort of the energy that we put toward things.
sentences.zh: 所以动机可以说是一种我们投入到事情中的能量。

sentences.en: It's where that energy comes from, what direction we're putting it in.
sentences.zh: 它是这种能量的来源，以及我们将其投入的方向。

sentences.en: And it's really a function of our own feelings and beliefs and attitudes and the way we approach different situations.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是我们的感受、信念、态度以及我们对待不同情境的方式的一种功能体现。

sentences.en: And motivation is really something that is inside of us.
sentences.zh: 动机确实是存在于我们内心的一种东西。

sentences.en: So motives are in us.
sentences.zh: 所以动机就在我们体内。

sentences.en: And so when we think about what motivates us, we kind of motivate ourselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考是什么激励了我们时，我们在某种程度上是在激励自己。

sentences.en: And that can be a function of what's in this situation.
sentences.zh: 这可能是情境中某种因素的作用。

sentences.en: So that's why we say in the book that you can get someone to do something.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们在书中说，你可以让某人去做一件事。

sentences.en: You can persuade them to do something.
sentences.zh: 你可以说服他们去做某事。

sentences.en: But you can't really get them to want to do something.
sentences.zh: 但你不能真正让他们想要去做某事。

sentences.en: You can't make people be motivated.
sentences.zh: 你无法强迫别人有动力。

sentences.en: Only you can set the conditions, but you can't make people be motivated.
sentences.zh: 只有你能设定条件，但你无法强迫别人产生动力。

sentences.en: They engage and energize from within.
sentences.zh: 他们是从内部产生参与感和精力的。

sentences.en: So that makes it kind of complex.
sentences.zh: 所以这让事情变得有点复杂。

sentences.en: It's not just as simple of getting people to do things.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是让人们去做事情那么简单。

sentences.en: It's inspiring the motives that they have within them to master things and persevere.
sentences.zh: 这是要激发他们内心的动机，让他们去掌握事物并坚持不懈。

sentences.en: And that makes it a little bit more complex.
sentences.zh: 这让事情变得更复杂了一些。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so I think one of the reasons why people think it's personality is because, as Wendy indicated, it's internal.
sentences.zh: 所以我想人们认为这是人格的原因之一是，正如温迪所指出的，它是内在的。

sentences.en: So it's coming from inside.
sentences.zh: 所以它是从内部发出的。

sentences.en: And so therefore, people assume it's a trait.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们认为它是一种特质。

sentences.en: You have it or you don't.
sentences.zh: 要么你有，要么你没有。

sentences.en: But it's that process, that energy, right, that in fact people have in some contexts versus others.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个过程，那种能量，对吧，事实上人们在某些情境下有，而在其他情境下没有。

sentences.en: I'm much more likely to get off the couch to eat cheesecake than I am to do exercise.
sentences.zh: 我为了吃芝士蛋糕而从沙发上起来的可能性，远大于我去锻炼身体的可能性。

sentences.en: Well, then if you're the parent of a young child, what can you do to create conditions that will help your child be motivated as a child and be motivated throughout life?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你是一个小孩子的家长，你能做些什么来创造条件，帮助你的孩子在童年时期乃至一生都充满动力呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: A lot of my work has focused on just that issue.
sentences.zh: 我的很多工作都集中在正是这个问题上。

sentences.en: So we start with the idea that people have these needs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从人们有这些需求的想法开始。

sentences.en: They have the need to feel autonomous, to feel, you know, they're the owner of their actions, like they're choosing to do things.
sentences.zh: 他们有感到自主的需求，去感觉，你知道的，他们是自己行为的主人，就像他们在选择做事一样。

sentences.en: They have a need to feel competent, to feel like they're good at things.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种感到胜任的需求，觉得他们擅长某些事情。

sentences.en: And they have a need to feel connected to other people.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种与他人建立联系的需求。

sentences.en: And so if we create an environment where people feel like they are the owner of their actions,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们创造一个环境，让人觉得他们是自己行为的主人，

sentences.en: like they have some choice, if we create an environment that helps them to feel effective, if we create an environment that helps them to feel connected to the people around them,
sentences.zh: 就像他们有一些选择权一样，如果我们创造一个环境帮助他们感到高效，如果我们创造一个环境帮助他们感到与周围的人有联系，

sentences.en: those are going to be the conditions under which people will be the most motivated.
sentences.zh: 这些将成为人们最具动力的条件。

sentences.en: So whether we're talking about the conditions that parents create or that classrooms create
sentences.zh: 因此，无论是我们谈论父母创造的条件、课堂创造的条件，

sentences.en: or that even bosses create in their workplaces, helping people to feel autonomous by providing
sentences.zh: 甚至是老板在工作场所创造的条件，通过向人们提供自主支持、支持他们的主动性并支持他们，给他们提供结构来帮助他们感到自主，

sentences.en: them autonomy support, support for their initiations and being behind them, giving them structure
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能感到胜任并知道对他们的期望是什么，同时感到被爱、被重视、被关怀和被尊重。

sentences.en: so that they can feel competent and know what they're expected to do and feeling loved and valued and cared for and respected.
sentences.zh: 这就是能够促进动机的整体环境。

sentences.en: That's the kind of overall environment that's going to facilitate motivation.
sentences.zh: 对于孩子，如果我们具体考虑孩子，父母与孩子关系的性质，

sentences.en: And in kids, if we think about kids specifically, the nature of the relationship that a parent has
sentences.zh: 将影响该孩子在参与父母想让他们做的事情时的动力有多大。

sentences.en: with their child is going to affect how motivated that child is in engaging with things that the parents want them to do.
sentences.zh: 课堂上也是如此。

sentences.en: The same thing occurs in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一个与学生关系不好的老师，比起学生喜欢老师、享受老师的课堂，其学生的动力可能会更少。

sentences.en: A teacher, in fact, who does not have a good relationship with their students is likely to have less
sentences.zh: 如果我们特别考虑到小孩子，这种胜任感，也就是说，把他们能做的事情或者刚好超出他们能力范围的事情摆在他们面前，这样如果他们努力就能成功，这就是你想要做的事情，因为这能建立胜任感。

sentences.en: motivated students than a classroom where the teachers, the students love the teacher, they enjoy the teacher.
sentences.zh: 温迪谈到的第三点是自主性。

sentences.en: And if we think about young kids in particular, this idea of competence, so putting things that
sentences.zh: 几乎每一本育儿书都有相关内容，你知道的，你会听到这样的故事：你想穿红睡衣还是蓝睡衣？

sentences.en: they can do or that just be on their grasp so that if they try, they can succeed is something that you want to do because that builds up the sense of competence.
sentences.zh: 这实际上完全源于自主性的概念，即给孩子选择权。

sentences.en: And the third point when he talks about was autonomy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有限的选择，但终究是选择。

sentences.en: Every parenting book practically has something about, you know, you hear the story about do you want to wear your red pajamas or your blue pajamas.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了他们一种控制感，从而会带来动力。

sentences.en: That actually is coming exactly out of this notion of autonomy, giving kids choice.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是为未来更大事情做准备的前期工作。

sentences.en: And so it's a limited choice, but it's choice nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 如果你能选择穿哪件睡衣，你或许就能选择去哪所大学。

sentences.en: And that gives them a sense of control, which then will be motivating.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So it's prep work also for bigger things to come.
sentences.zh: 事实上，想想我们国家拥有的最高水平的教育。

sentences.en: If you can choose which pajamas to wear, you might be able to choose which college to go to.
sentences.zh: 博士生可以选择他们的学位论文要做什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 所以事实上，这种选择的概念真的非常非常关键，并且在整个人生中发挥着作用。

sentences.en: And indeed, think about the highest levels of education that we have in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈奖励。

sentences.en: Doctoral students choose what they're going to do their dissertation on, right?
sentences.zh: 这种想法非常普遍，你可能会承诺给自己一个奖励，作为完成工作中的一项困难任务的激励，或者父母可能会给孩子现金，你知道的，为了成绩单上的全A。

sentences.en: So that in fact, this idea of choice is really, really key and plays out throughout the lifespan.
sentences.zh: 像这样的奖励有用吗？

sentences.en: Let's talk about rewards.
sentences.zh: 它们能提高动机吗？

sentences.en: This idea is really common that you might promise yourself a treat as an incentive to finishing a difficult task at work, or parent might offer their child cash, you know, for
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个好问题，金。

sentences.en: an A on a report card.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在书中经常讨论的事情。

sentences.en: Do rewards like this work?
sentences.zh: 答案是它很复杂。

sentences.en: Do they increase motivation?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当然可以通过足够大的奖励让我的孩子打扫房间，或者如果老板给出足够大的奖励，他可以让他的一名员工在周六来上班。

sentences.en: You know, that's a great question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 奖励的问题在于，当你因为某事而给某人奖励时，他们产生了一种外在的动机。

sentences.en: It's something we talk a lot about in our book.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为了得到奖励而去做它。

sentences.en: And the answer is it's complex.
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得没有选择的余地。

sentences.en: You know, I certainly could, with a big enough reward, I could get my child to clean their
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得自己在被那个奖励所控制。

sentences.en: room, or if the boss gives a big enough reward, he can get his employee to come in on a Saturday.
sentences.zh: 他们可能想要得到那个奖励。

sentences.en: The problem with rewards is that when you give someone a reward for doing something, they have a sense of motivation that's external.
sentences.zh: 但这样做所做的是，它削弱了为了做这件事本身的乐趣或是为了做这件事的重要性而去做的动机。

sentences.en: It's where I'm doing it to get the reward.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你说，例如，如果你吃掉你的，如果你吃掉豌豆，你就可以得到甜点。

sentences.en: It makes them feel not choiceful.
sentences.zh: 这真的贬低了那些豌豆的价值。

sentences.en: It makes them feel like they are being controlled by that reward.
sentences.zh: 而且，你只有在得到甜点的情况下才会吃那些豌豆。

sentences.en: And they might want to get that reward.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，特别是对孩子来说，我们努力做的事情不仅仅是让孩子做事情。

sentences.en: But what it does is it takes away from the doing of the activity for the either joy of doing it or for the importance of doing it even.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: So if you say, for example, if you eat your, if you eat your peas, you can get dessert.
sentences.zh: 而是要让孩子重视事情并发现它们很重要。

sentences.en: It really devalues those peas.
sentences.zh: 当你把重点放在那个外部奖励上时，你就会把它保持在那个水平。

sentences.en: And it's, you would only eat those peas if you got dessert.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们没有去理解打扫房间的价值或家庭作业的价值，结果发生的是人们觉得我在做这件事。

sentences.en: And a lot of times, particularly with kids, what we're trying to do is not just get kids to do things.
sentences.zh: 我只有为了得到奖励才会这样做。

sentences.en: We can do that.
sentences.zh: 这本身没有什么价值，而如果你和孩子们一起工作，帮助他们理解他们正在做的事情的价值，并与他们一起找出它如何能满足他们的目标，

sentences.en: But get kids to value things and to find them important.
sentences.zh: 他们会将其内化并开始做这件事，因为这很重要。

sentences.en: And when you focus on that external reward, you're keeping it at that level.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们要求孩子做的事情、要求员工做的事情中，可能确实有些是一次性的事情，它们本身并没有什么真正的价值。

sentences.en: So instead of helping kids to understand the value of cleaning their rooms or the value of homework, what ends up happening is that people feel like I'm doing this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那你就会问，那我们为什么要让人们去做没有价值的事情呢？

sentences.en: I would only do this to get the reward.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，奖励可以让他们去做。

sentences.en: That's, it's not valuable in and of itself versus if you're working with kids and helping them to understand the value of what they're doing and working with them to figure out how
sentences.zh: 但当它是一件重要的事情，是一件我们希望人们继续做下去、我们希望人们重视、我们希望人们真正全力以赴的事情时，奖励可能会产生反作用。

sentences.en: it can meet their goals.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一整统的研究表明，当人们在做他们喜欢的事情时，你把他们带到实验室里，他们在做一个非常有趣的课题，然后你说，嘿，你做的每一个拼图或者你组装的每一个小部件，我们都会付钱给你。

sentences.en: They're going to internalize that and start to do the thing because it's important.
sentences.zh: 他们会将其内化，并开始付诸实践，因为这很重要。

sentences.en: Now, there probably are some things that we ask kids to do, that we ask our employees to do that are just one-timers that are not really valuable in and of themselves.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们要求孩子们做的事情、要求员工做的事情中，可能确实有一些是一次性的，它们本身并没有什么真正的价值。

sentences.en: Well, then you're asking, so why are we asking people to do things that are not valuable?
sentences.zh: 那么，你就会问了，既然如此，我们为什么还要要求人们去做那些没有价值的事情呢？

sentences.en: But anyway, and the reward can get them to do it.
sentences.zh: 不过无论如何，奖励确实能让他们去完成。

sentences.en: But when it's something important and it's something that we want people to continue to do, we want people to value, we want people to really get behind, rewards can undermine.
sentences.zh: 但当这是一件重要的事情，是我们希望人们继续做下去、希望人们重视、希望人们真正全力支持的事情时，奖励反而会起反作用。

sentences.en: So there's a whole tradition of research that's shown that when people are doing something
sentences.zh: 因此，有一整套研究传统表明，当人们在做某件事情时——

sentences.en: they love, you bring them into the laboratory, they're doing a really fun task and you say, hey, we're going to pay you for every one of these puzzles you're doing or every one
sentences.zh: 他们热爱这件事，你把他们带到实验室里，他们在做一个非常有趣的维吾尔任务，然后你对他们说：嘿，你们每解开一个这样的谜题，或者每完成一个

sentences.en: of these widgets you put together.
sentences.zh: 这样的部件，我们都会付钱给你们。

sentences.en: And then they're like, great.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会觉得，太棒了。

sentences.en: They do more of them.
sentences.zh: 他们会做更多。

sentences.en: They do more puzzles.
sentences.zh: 他们会做更多益智拼图。

sentences.en: They do more widgets.
sentences.zh: 他们会做更多小玩意。

sentences.en: Then you say, oh, the experiment's over.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，哦，实验结束了。

sentences.en: We're done.
sentences.zh: 我们完成了。

sentences.en: I'm going to go out and you can do some more puzzles or you can do something else.
sentences.zh: 我要出去了，你可以再做几个拼图，或者做点别的。

sentences.en: The people that were rewarded do less of the puzzles or make less widgets because their motivation has been transformed into something they do to get money.
sentences.zh: 得到奖励的人反而做的拼图变少了，或者做的小玩意变少了，因为他们的动机已经变成了为了赚钱而做。

sentences.en: And so that sense of, I do it because it's interesting and fun is taken away.
sentences.zh: 因此，“我因为有趣和好玩而去做”的那种感觉就被剥夺了。

sentences.en: You've now sort of turned fun into work.
sentences.zh: 你现在有点把乐趣变成了工作。

sentences.en: And so the nuance there is, yes, you can probably use rewards to get people to do some things,
sentences.zh: 所以这里的微妙之处在于，是的，你可能可以用奖励来让人去做某些事，

sentences.en: but be very careful with them because if it's fun things and interesting things, you'll take away the fun and the intereSt.
sentences.zh: 但对它们要非常小心，因为如果是好玩和有趣的事情，你会剥夺其中的乐趣和兴趣。

sentences.en: And if it's things that are valuable, you'll prevent people from sort of moving along a continuum from doing things because they have to, to doing things because they want to.
sentences.zh: 如果是那些有价值的事情，你会阻止人们沿着一条连续的轨迹前进——从不得不做某事，到因为想做而去做。

sentences.en: So it's a, it's sort of a very nuanced thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种，这是一种非常微妙的事情。

sentences.en: It sounds like it can have exactly the opposite effect of what, what you want.
sentences.zh: 听起来它产生的作用可能恰好与你想要的相反。

sentences.en: So it decreases motivation ultimately.
sentences.zh: 所以它最终会降低动机。

sentences.en: Ultimately.
sentences.zh: 最终。

sentences.en: So it can really backfire.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的会适得其反。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so if we think about the example that you asked, for instance, the parent who decides to pay the kids for grades, well, that's fine when they can afford to do so.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们想想你刚才问的那个例子，比如决定为孩子的成绩付钱给他们的父母，嗯，当他们付得起时这倒没问题。

sentences.en: But when they actually cannot afford to do so, then the kid may stop working.
sentences.zh: 但当他们实际上付不起时，孩子可能就不干了。

sentences.en: When the kid goes on to college, are they going to do the work in college if they're not getting paid for the grade?
sentences.zh: 当孩子上大学时，如果他们拿不到成绩奖金，他们还会在大学里用功吗？

sentences.en: Because again, as Wendy pointed out, it's now become, I'm doing it for the reward rather than doing it for the value or the interest that I have in the task.
sentences.zh: 因为正如温迪所指出的，现在它变成了一切为了奖励，而不是为了我对这项任务本身的价值或兴趣。

sentences.en: There's a lot of discussion out there in the world about whether parents and teachers should tell kids that they're smart.
sentences.zh: 世面上有很多关于父母和老师是否应该告诉孩子他们很聪明的讨论。

sentences.en: And I just want to know, what about praise?
sentences.zh: 我只想知道，表扬呢？

sentences.en: How does praise affect motivation?
sentences.zh: 表扬如何影响动机？

sentences.en: Well, you know, this is something that in fact has gotten into the school system.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这实际上已经进入了学校系统。

sentences.en: I think a lot recently it's related to attribution theory, you know, the reasons why we do things.
sentences.zh: 我想最近有很多这方面的内容，它与归因理论有关，你知道的，也就是我们做某事的原因。

sentences.en: And when we tell a kid that you have done well, you are smart, right, that that's why you've
sentences.zh: 当我们告诉一个孩子，你做得很好，你很聪明，没错，这就是你

sentences.en: been successful, we've actually set the bar that in fact you have this thick, this smartness that's fixed, and so therefore that's why you did well.
sentences.zh: 成功的原因，我们实际上就设定了这样一个标准：事实上，你拥有这种恒定的聪明才智，所以这就是你做得好的原因。

sentences.en: Well, every person is going to come to a point where there's something that they will do that will be difficult or they will have a failure experience.
sentences.zh: 好吧，每个人都会遇到这样一个时刻：他们要做的事情会变得很困难，或者他们会经历一次失败。

sentences.en: If in fact they think that their success is due to the fact that it's because they're smart, when they have a failure experience, it's easy for them to then think,
sentences.zh: 如果他们真的认为自己的成功是因为自己聪明，当他们经历失败时，他们很容易就会认为：

sentences.en: I have lost my smarts, my smarts have gone away.
sentences.zh: 我变笨了，我的聪明才智消失了。

sentences.en: And so what happens, rather than engaging, right, continuing to put more effort,
sentences.zh: 所以会发生什么呢？他们不会继续投入，不会继续付出更多努力，

sentences.en: then they are likely to disengage, to become demotivated.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们很可能会退缩，变得失去动力。

sentences.en: If instead we praise them for the process, you know, you worked really hard on this project
sentences.zh: 如果我们转而为他们的过程表扬他们，你知道的，你在这个项目上付出了巨大的努力，

sentences.en: and look how it paid off, then what we are setting up is that in fact, not that you are smart,
sentences.zh: 看看它是如何得到回报的，那么我们建立的观念就不是“你很聪明”，

sentences.en: but that the thing that you can control, your effort, is what's setting you up, you know.
sentences.zh: 而是你可以控制的东西——你的努力——才是成就你的关键，你知道的。

sentences.en: And so this then, in fact, allows them to continue.
sentences.zh: 因此，这实际上能让他们坚持下去。

sentences.en: And this is particularly important in every education context, which applies in work, because as you go up the grade levels, things get more difficult, right?
sentences.zh: 这在任何教育背景下都尤别重要，这也适用于工作，因为随着年级升高，事情变得越来越难，对吧？

sentences.en: So you are inevitably going to get to a place where there's something that does not come as easily as the previous task did.
sentences.zh: 所以你不可避免地会遇到这样一个阶段：有些事情不会像以前的任务那样轻易就能完成。

sentences.en: What about competition?
sentences.zh: 竞争呢？

sentences.en: You know, it might seem intuitive that if a student is studying for a spelling bee at school or an employee is aiming to win a competitive promotion,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这可能很符合直觉：如果一个学生正在为学校的拼字比赛而学习，或者一个员工正致力于赢得一场竞争激烈的晋升，

sentences.en: that they'll be more motivated to work harder.
sentences.zh: 他们就会更有动力去更努力地工作。

sentences.en: Is that a reality or is that a myth?
sentences.zh: 这是一个现实，还是一个神话？

sentences.en: It turns out that, you know, competition, one can think of competition as one end of a continuum and cooperation.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，你知道的，竞争，人们可以把竞争看作是一个连续体的一端，另一端是合作。

sentences.en: Now, we know they're separate now.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道它们是分开的了。

sentences.en: But for a lot of the early research, look at competition versus cooperation.
sentences.zh: 但在早期的很多研究中，人们都是将竞争与合作进行对比。

sentences.en: And what we found is that, in fact, when, in fact, competition and cooperation are directly put against each other, cooperation wins all the time, hands down, right?
sentences.zh: 我们发现，事实上，当竞争和合作被直接放在一起对立时，合作每次都稳操胜券，毫无悬念，对吧？

sentences.en: Because competition becomes almost some of the things we've talked about before.
sentences.zh: 因为竞争几乎变成了我们之前谈到的一些事情。

sentences.en: It becomes controlling.
sentences.zh: 它变得具有控制性。

sentences.en: I'm doing it just to win.
sentences.zh: 我这么做只是为了赢。

sentences.en: But there are other things to think about.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他事情需要考虑。

sentences.en: There are different competitive orientations.
sentences.zh: 存在不同的竞争取向。

sentences.en: So people have different competitive orientations.
sentences.zh: 所以人们有不同的竞争取向。

sentences.en: So there are some people who are hyper-competitive.
sentences.zh: 有些人极度好胜。

sentences.en: They want to win at all costs.
sentences.zh: 他们不惜一切代价想要赢。

sentences.en: And so these people will always make things into competition, but they may also stray over into being unethical to win.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人总是会把事情变成竞争，但他们为了赢也可能会越界做出不道德的事。

sentences.en: Because winning, it doesn't matter what you do once you win.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦能赢，你做什么都无所谓了。

sentences.en: I think we can think about politicians, and we can certainly think of many scandals in the sporting arena over the past few decades where that has played out.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以想到政客，过去几十年来，我们当然也能想到体育界发生的许多丑闻，在那些事情中这一点展现得淋漓尽致。

sentences.en: But there are also people who are the type of competition that, in fact, is perhaps most useful is what we call self-developmental competition.
sentences.zh: 但也有这样一种人，他们所参与的这种竞争——实际上也许是最有用的一种——被称为自我发展型竞争。

sentences.en: So people who see competition not just as a chance to win, but as a chance to grow.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人把竞争不仅看作是一个获胜的机会，更看作是一个成长的机会。

sentences.en: So that, in fact, I am pacing myself.
sentences.zh: 所以事实上，我在按自己的节奏前进。

sentences.en: And so I did, I ran this thing in 15 seconds.
sentences.zh: 比如我以15秒完成了这个项目。

sentences.en: I'm making it up.
sentences.zh: 我这是瞎编的。

sentences.en: Before, I've done it in 14 on this trial.
sentences.zh: 之前我在这次尝试中用了14秒。

sentences.en: So that, in fact, what I'm doing as a competition is really a way for me to understand, am I mastering the material, you know, and how am I improving?
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我所进行的竞争真的是为了让我明白：我是否掌握了这些材料，你知道的，我是如何改进的？

sentences.en: And we found that there are people who have that sort of orientation, that for them, competition is not as demotivating.
sentences.zh: 我们发现有些人有这种取向，对他们来说，竞争并不会那么消磨积极性。

sentences.en: Because if they do not win, they have still sometimes, they've learned something about their performance.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们没有赢，他们有时仍然能从中学到关于自己表现的一些东西。

sentences.en: And the other thing that we found is not just individual.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的另一件事不仅仅是个体层面的。

sentences.en: But these competitive attitudes differ across cultures.
sentences.zh: 而且这些竞争态度因文化而异。

sentences.en: So, for example, in Japan, they're much more likely to think as competitors, as individuals who are helping them pace themselves, whereas in some of the Western countries,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如在日本，他们更有可能把竞争对手看作是帮助自己调整节奏的个人，而在一些西方国家，

sentences.en: competitors are people to be beaten, to be trounced.
sentences.zh: 竞争对手则是必须被击败、被狠狠践踏的人。

sentences.en: And so it really does depend on the orientation that you take towards competition.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实取决于你对竞争采取的取向。

sentences.en: And I think Wendy may have a few things to add here.
sentences.zh: 我想温迪可能有些话要补充。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll just add a little bit.
sentences.zh: 是的，我只补充一点。

sentences.en: And I mean, we're saying that competition can have some negative effects for some people in some contexts, but a lot of times it's how we present the competition.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们一直在说竞争在某些语境下会对某些人产生一些负面影响，但很多时候这取决于我们如何呈现竞争。

sentences.en: So, for example, in a tennis game, it's a competitive game.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如在一场网球比赛中，这是一场竞争性的比赛。

sentences.en: You want to hit it so that your opponent can't get it.
sentences.zh: 你想把球打过去，让你的对手接不到。

sentences.en: By nature, it's a competitive game.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，这是一场竞争游戏。

sentences.en: But you can come into that game and focus solely on winning.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以带着“纯粹为了赢”的心态去参加比赛。

sentences.en: That's all that matters.
sentences.zh: 那才是唯一重要的事。

sentences.en: And when you're so narrowly focused on winning, it actually undermines your motivation.
sentences.zh: 当你如此狭隘地专注于获胜时，它实际上会削弱你的动力。

sentences.en: And it actually undermines your game sometimes because you're so focused on winning that your strokes aren't smooth.
sentences.zh: 有时它甚至会毁了你的发挥，因为你太专注于获胜，导致挥拍不够流畅。

sentences.en: You're so narrowed in.
sentences.zh: 你的视野变得太局限了。

sentences.en: Rather than having fun and also bettering your skills, as Frank was talking about.
sentences.zh: 而不是像弗兰克刚才谈到的那样，去享受乐趣并提高技能。

sentences.en: So, what we can do in situations that are competitive, let's say our children are paying competitive soccer, is not focus so much on winning.
sentences.zh: 所以，在竞争激烈的环境中，比方说我们的孩子在踢竞争激烈的足球时，我们可以做的是不要把注意力过多地放在获胜上。

sentences.en: Focus a little bit more on whether the kids enjoyed the game, how they feel they played.
sentences.zh: 更多地关注孩子们是否享受比赛，以及他们对自己的表现有何感受。

sentences.en: Instead of when your child comes home saying, who won?
sentences.zh: 而不是当你的孩子回家时问：谁赢了？

sentences.en: You know, that's for that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是那样。

sentences.en: Then they get their ego involved in winning.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就会把好胜心（自我）纠缠在输赢上。

sentences.en: Then they feel like I'm not good enough if I don't win versus I'm really here to enjoy the game.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会觉得，如果没赢，我就不够好，这与“我真的是来享受比赛的”截然不同。

sentences.en: And lots of times kids start playing whatever sport they're playing to really enjoy it and then get ego involved like that because there's too much focus on winning.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，孩子们开始玩他们玩的任何运动真的是为了享受乐趣，然后由于对获胜的关注度过高，才沾染了这种争强好胜的心理。

sentences.en: So, how we set it up.
sentences.zh: 所以，关键在于我们如何去设定它。

sentences.en: My daughter actually had a tennis coach who would ask her at the end of tournament, how'd it go?
sentences.zh: 我女儿实际上有一个网球教练，在比赛结束时会问她：战况如何？

sentences.en: And she'd say, I won.
sentences.zh: 她会说：我赢了。

sentences.en: And he'd say, dynamite.
sentences.zh: 他会说：太棒了。

sentences.en: And she'd say, I loSt.
sentences.zh: 她会说：我输了。

sentences.en: And he'd say, did you have fun?
sentences.zh: 他会说：你玩得开心吗？

sentences.en: And she said, yep.
sentences.zh: 她说：嗯。

sentences.en: And he said, dynamite.
sentences.zh: 他说：太棒了。

sentences.en: So, it's really, it's not just the competition of a situation.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实，不仅仅是某种情况下的竞争。

sentences.en: It's how it's portrayed.
sentences.zh: 关键在于它是如何被诠释的。

sentences.en: You know, if it's all about winning, it has that effect that, especially when you lose,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果一切只为了赢，它就会产生那种效果——特别是当你输了的时候，

sentences.en: it really can undermine your motivation and just like it's too much pressure and it doesn't feel good and it loses its fun.
sentences.zh: 它真的会消磨你的动力，就像压力太大，感觉不好，并失去了乐趣一样。

sentences.en: So, on the one hand, you're saying that you can't inspire, you can't make people motivated.
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面，你是在说你无法激励他人，无法让人产生动力。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, I'm hearing you say that there are things you can say that maybe will enhance their own motivation.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，我听到你说有些话是可以说的，也许这能增强他们自身的动力。

sentences.en: Is that what we're talking about here?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在这里讨论的内容吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: You can set up a situation where people have what they need to succeed.
sentences.zh: 你可以创造这样一种情境：人们拥有他们成功所需的一切。

sentences.en: They know the guidelines.
sentences.zh: 他们知道准则。

sentences.en: They know the expectations.
sentences.zh: 他们知道期望。

sentences.en: They have some say in it.
sentences.zh: 他们对此有发言权。

sentences.en: They have feel, you set it up so they feel like they have some choice in it.
sentences.zh: 他们有这种感觉——你营造出一种氛围，让他们觉得自己在其中有一定的自主选择权。

sentences.en: They're connected to the people around them.
sentences.zh: 他们与周围的人紧密相连。

sentences.en: You can set up those situations and a context like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以创造出这样的情境和上下文。

sentences.en: And people will then want to persevere.
sentences.zh: 人们就会想要坚持下去。

sentences.en: They will want to try to master things and they won't get their ego so involved in it and they won't feel so pressured.
sentences.zh: 他们会想要努力掌握事物，不会把过多的好胜心（自我）牵扯其中，也不会感到那么大压力。

sentences.en: So, you definitely can set up a classroom or a team or a home that has high expectations but also is not pressured and has a sense of valuing people's own goals and what they're
sentences.zh: 所以，你绝对可以建立一个这样的课堂、团队或家庭：它有很高的期望，但同时也没有压力，并且有一种价值观，尊重人们自己的目标以及他们

sentences.en: trying to do and not putting pressure on them to win at all costs.
sentences.zh: 努力去做的事情，而不是给他们施加不惜一切代价去赢的压力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I would add that when we think about competition, competition has a long history.
sentences.zh: 我要补充的是，当我们思考竞争时，竞争有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: In fact, it probably has been around as long as humans have had the cognitive capacity that we've had.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它存在的历史可能和人类拥有现有认知能力的历史一样长。

sentences.en: When you think of the Olympic Games, they go back to ancient Greece and why is it still with us?
sentences.zh: 当你想到奥林匹克运动会时，它们可以追溯到古希腊，为什么它至今仍然存在？

sentences.en: So, inevitably, competition is present in society and when somebody wins, others lose, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，竞争在社会中是不可避免的，当有人获胜时，其他人就会失败，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, they get feedback.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们会得到反馈。

sentences.en: When you get feedback, negative feedback, you've not won, it's easy to be demotivated.
sentences.zh: 当你得到反馈，尤其是负面反馈——你没有赢时，很容易失去动力。

sentences.en: And so, even in the context with regard to your question of somebody who did not win, the way you provide the feedback can be useful in helping them maintain motivation, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，即便是在针对你提出的“有人没有赢”的这个问题的情境下，你提供反馈的方式也有助于帮助他们保持动力，对吧？

sentences.en: By giving them change feedback, doing it privately, empathetically, giving them choices in their strategy to move forward.
sentences.zh: 通过给予他们关于改变的反馈，私下里、充满同理心地进行，在他们前进的策略中给予他们选择。

sentences.en: So, when we think about the, you know, we have these negative examples of people at the sidelines
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们想到——你知道的，我们看到赛场边有些负面的例子，

sentences.en: shouting nasty comments at their children or at their players when, in fact, something has not gone the way of that particular team or that particular individual.
sentences.zh: 当某个特定的团队或个人表现不尽如人意时，他们对自己的孩子或队员大喊大叫，发表恶劣的言论。

sentences.en: Those kinds of, that kind of feedback is not very helpful for motivation, right?
sentences.zh: 那种，那种反馈对激发动力一点帮助也没有，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, things, people may end up performing, but they are, again, doing it under coercion.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们最终可能会去表现，但他们同样是在胁迫下进行的。

sentences.en: They're not having fun.
sentences.zh: 他们并不快乐。

sentences.en: They are likely to, their performance is likely to decrease over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们的表现很可能会下降。

sentences.en: Whereas, if in point of fact, you are getting empathetic, supportive feedback, things that can better you, help you get better at doing the task, you are acting, and, you know, you
sentences.zh: 然而，事实上，如果你得到的是富有同理心的、支持性的反馈，那些能够让你变得更好、帮你更好地完成任务的事情，你就会付诸行动，并且，你知道的，

sentences.en: don't lose the enjoyment that you have while you were doing this in the first place, and you're going to continue down that road.
sentences.zh: 你不会失去你最初做这件事时所拥有的快乐，并且你会沿着这条路继续走下去。

sentences.en: Now, another myth that you discuss in the book is the idea that if you visualize success, it will come.
sentences.zh: 现在，你在书中讨论的另一个神话是：如果你设想成功，成功就会到来。

sentences.en: Why is that a myth?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是一个神话？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you need to do then instead of visualizing success?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果不去设想成功，你接下来需要做什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's, that's one that's really out there in the media.
sentences.zh: 是的，这在媒体上确实非常盛行。

sentences.en: If you go on, if you Google, you know, yeah, visualize yourself at the top of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 如果你去上网搜索，你知道的，就会看到“想象你自己站在山顶上”。

sentences.en: And so, it turns out that there's a lot of research, some of it by Gabrielle Ottingen and
sentences.zh: 结果证明，有很多研究，其中一些由加布里埃尔·奥廷根和其他人开展，

sentences.en: other people, to show that if you visualize the outcome, it's kind of like your mind thinks you've done it, and you don't really have put energy toward the task as much, as if
sentences.zh: 表明如果你把结果可视化，这就好比你的大脑认为你已经做到了，于是你对任务投入的精力，其实不如你去可视化

sentences.en: you visualize the sort of process of getting there, the steps that you need to get there.
sentences.zh: 到达那里的过程、你需要采取的步骤时那么多。

sentences.en: It sort of energizes you to move forward, and it also gives you the information you need to reach that goal.
sentences.zh: 这会激励你前进，并且它还能为你提供实现该目标所需的信息。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's definitely a myth that you should visualize, you know, running across the finish
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，认为自己应该想象自己冲过终点线，这绝对是一个神话；

sentences.en: line, it's really better to visualize the steps you need to take, like every morning, getting up, turning your alarm clock on, going out for a run, and practicing, and figuring
sentences.zh: 最好还是想象你需要采取的步骤，比如每天早上起床、设好闹钟、出去跑步、练习，并弄清楚

sentences.en: out how many miles you need to go each time, and so forth, and setting these smaller goals,
sentences.zh: 每次你需要跑多少英里等等，设定这些较小的目标，并通过这样的话来为事情做真正的计划：

sentences.en: and really planning for things by saying, you know, if it's six o'clock in the morning,
sentences.zh: “如果现在是早上六点……”

sentences.en: I'll be out there running.
sentences.zh: 我会出门跑步。

sentences.en: It gives you a plan.
sentences.zh: 它为你提供了一个计划。

sentences.en: It energizes you for each of the steps.
sentences.zh: 它为你每一步行动注入活力。

sentences.en: You can plan for all the distractions that might come in your way that will prevent you from doing it, and that's a much better plan than visualizing the end point.
sentences.zh: 你可以为可能阻碍你行动的各种干扰提前做好计划，这比单纯想象终点要好得多。

sentences.en: You know, I think in society, we see final products.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为在社会中，我们看到的是最终的产品。

sentences.en: We see a Beyonce or Taylor Swift concert.
sentences.zh: 我们看到碧昂丝或泰勒·斯威夫特的演唱会。

sentences.en: We see Steph Curry in the basketball court, and it seems so easy, right?
sentences.zh: 我们在篮球场上看到斯蒂芬·库里，这看起来太容易了，对吧？

sentences.en: And so this idea of this, oh, you're shooting this beautiful three-point shot, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这种想法，哦，你在投那个漂亮的三分球，对吧？

sentences.en: And so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: What we don't see is the hard work from where this person was to this easy performance on the stage or on the basketball court or the football field.
sentences.zh: 我们看不到的是这个人从过去走到舞台、篮球场或足球场上那轻松表现背后的艰辛努力。

sentences.en: And that is why the visualizing itself can't work, because the visualizing jumps over the hard work.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么单纯的可视化无法发挥作用，因为可视化跳过了艰辛的努力。

sentences.en: And so what, in fact, you should visualize, in fact, how are you going to put in the work to get to that final goal?
sentences.zh: 事实上，你应该去可视化的，其实是你将如何付出努力去实现那个最终目标？

sentences.en: But what about the reverse?
sentences.zh: 但反过来呢？

sentences.en: I mean, when I played softball, for example, you know, the coach would say, don't visualize yourself dropping the ball.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如当我打垒球时，你知道的，教练会说，不要想象自己把球漏接了。

sentences.en: You have to visualize yourself catching that ball in the outfield.
sentences.zh: 你必须想象自己在场外接住了那个球。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't there some truth that if you imagine that you're going to miss the ball, you're going to miss the ball?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道没有这样一种道理：如果你想象自己会接不到球，你就会接不到球吗？

sentences.en: I think that, in fact, we know that there are things called self-fulfilling prophecies.
sentences.zh: 我认为，事实上，我们知道有一种东西叫做自证预言。

sentences.en: If you visualize yourself dropping the ball, you are likely to increase your anxiety and so forth.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象自己把球漏接了，你很可能会增加焦虑，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, so that's fine.
sentences.zh: 所以，因此，这倒也无所谓。

sentences.en: So you don't want to visualize yourself dropping the ball.
sentences.zh: 所以你并不想想象自己把球漏接了。

sentences.en: You don't want to set up conditions that are going to make, in fact, your cognitive capacity diminish.
sentences.zh: 你不想设定那些实际上会使你的认知能力下降的条件。

sentences.en: At the same time, if you visualize yourself catching the ball without practicing catching that ball, you're not going to catch it either.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，如果你在没有练习接球的情况下想象自己接住了球，你也是接不住的。

sentences.en: And so that's why visualize yourself catching the ball, but you visualize yourself practicing catching those ball on multiple occasions.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你要想象自己接住球，但你要想象自己多次练习接球的场景。

sentences.en: Now, another myth that you tackle is that if you're motivated, you'll be successful.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们驳斥的另一个迷思是：只要有动机，你就会成功。

sentences.en: Why is that a myth?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是一个迷思？

sentences.en: I mean, is motivation alone just not enough?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，单靠动机难道还不够吗？

sentences.en: We're motivated to do a lot of things that we don't end up doing.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多事情都很有动力去做，但最终却没有去做。

sentences.en: You know, we say we're going to, we're really motivated to clean that attic up and it's really important, you know, to us and we never quite get to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们说我们要去，我们真的很有动力去清理那个阁楼，这对我们来说真的很重要，你知道的，但我们总是没去弄。

sentences.en: So for things that, particularly for things that are difficult, we need to have also a plan.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于那些困难的事情，特别是对于困难的事情，我们需要有一个计划。

sentences.en: We need to have put into place what we call implementation intentions.
sentences.zh: 我们需要落实我们所说的执行意图。

sentences.en: We need to put into place if, you know, statements such as if-then statements to say, you know, if it's Saturday and it's five o'clock, I'm going to start doing that attic.
sentences.zh: 我们需要落实诸如“如果-那么”之类的陈述，比如，你知道的，如果今天是星期六，到了五点钟，我就要开始清理那个阁楼。

sentences.en: I'm going to do it for X amount of time.
sentences.zh: 我要花特定的时间来做这件事。

sentences.en: And so really putting into place some plans and some plans also for being distracted.
sentences.zh: 所以，确实要制定一些计划，还要为可能受到的干扰制定一些计划。

sentences.en: If the phone rings, I'm not going to stop cleaning the attic.
sentences.zh: 如果电话响了，我不会停止清理阁楼。

sentences.en: So having motivation is a great thing, but you also need to follow that up with some plans.
sentences.zh: 所以有动机是一件好事，但你也需要用一些计划来跟进。

sentences.en: The opposite is also a little bit true.
sentences.zh: 反过来其实也有一点道理。

sentences.en: So sometimes for things that we, we don't really feel that motivated for, but we, what we need to do, we can make those plans and we will find if we follow them, it's actually
sentences.zh: 所以有时候对于那些我们其实没有太大动力，但又必须去做的事情，我们可以制定计划，而且我们会发现，如果我们照着去做，其实

sentences.en: not nearly as bad as we thought it was going to be.
sentences.zh: 并没有我们想象的那么糟糕。

sentences.en: So we just need to get, so we say in our book, we say, just do something, anything.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只需要开始，正如我们在书中所说，我们说，去做点什么吧，什么都行。

sentences.en: If you're, if you're feeling like, you know, you're writing a paper and you can't really get yourself up to do much, you don't have a whole lot of energy, just do the references,
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得，你知道的，你正在写一篇论文，却实在提不起劲做太多事，没有太多精力，那就只管写参考文献，

sentences.en: just do a few little things.
sentences.zh: 只管做一些小事情。

sentences.en: So do something because once you start, it can really get you rolling and, and people anticipate that things are going to be much worse than they actually are.
sentences.zh: 所以去做点什么吧，因为一旦你开始，它就能让你真正运转起来，而且人们往往会把事情预想得比实际情况糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Even for negative tasks, things that you don't want to do, they're, they're actually tend to be that cleaning that attic was not really as bad as, as you thought it was going to
sentences.zh: 即使是对于消极的任务、你不想做的事情，它们其实往往——清理阁楼其实并没有你想象的那么

sentences.en: be.
sentences.zh: 糟。

sentences.en: It was actually kind of enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 事实上还挺愉快的。

sentences.en: So, you also bust the myth around the idea that structure damages motivation, that there
sentences.zh: 所以，你们也打破了关于“结构会损害动机”的迷思，即有些人认为

sentences.en: are some people who think that they're, they'll be too restricted if there's a structure around what it is that they need to do.
sentences.zh: 如果对他们需要做的事情周围有限制或结构，他们会感到束缚太多。

sentences.en: Why, why is this not true?
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么这不是真的？

sentences.en: You know, Kim, that we, we actually did a survey of, of people to asking them if they believe in these, these ideas.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，金，我们，我们实际上对人们做了一项调查，询问他们是否相信这些观点。

sentences.en: And a lot of people believe in a lot of these myths that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 很多人都相信我们正在讨论的这些迷思中的很多个。

sentences.en: The structure one, people like half the people said, I don't know, or, or didn't seem to really know they, um, because we don't really know what structure is.
sentences.zh: 关于结构的那一个，大约一半的人说，我不知道，或者，似乎真的不知道，嗯，因为我们真的不知道什么是结构。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, the, the problem is that a lot of times what people do is they pit structure against having like freedom that either you can have structure in your environment or
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，问题在于很多时候人们所做的是将结构对立于自由，认为要么你的环境中可以有结构，要么

sentences.en: you feel controlled.
sentences.zh: 你就会觉得被控制。

sentences.en: And really there are two kind of two separate dimensions.
sentences.zh: 而实际上这是两种截然不同的维度。

sentences.en: There's how much structure there is in the environment, how clear the rules and expectations are about what you're supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 一个是环境中有多少结构，关于你应该做什么的规则和期望有多清晰。

sentences.en: Um, the boundaries, you know, we live in a world, there's, there's structure all around us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那些界限，你知道的，我们生活在一个世界里，到处都是结构。

sentences.en: You know, we, there's rules and expectations.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们有规则和期望。

sentences.en: We can't drive through a red light and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们不能闯红灯，等等。

sentences.en: Those are just the, it's the way the world is.
sentences.zh: 这些只是，这是世界的运作方式。

sentences.en: Um, and then there's how that structure is imposed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后就是这种结构是如何施加的。

sentences.en: Is it imposed in a way that feels controlling and pushy where you don't have any say in it?
sentences.zh: 它是以一种让你觉得被控制、被逼迫、让你没有任何发言权的方式施加的吗？

sentences.en: Um, or is it structure that's imposed in a way that you can have a, uh, have a role in, in thinking about it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，还是说这种结构的施加方式，能让你在其中扮演一个角色、参与思考？

sentences.en: You can put in your input.
sentences.zh: 你可以提出你的意见。

sentences.en: And so structure facilitates people being competent.
sentences.zh: 因此，结构有助于人们变得更有能力。

sentences.en: So that's really good for motivation.
sentences.zh: 所以这对动机真的很好。

sentences.en: If you don't know what you're supposed to do on your assignment, um, you're going to feel helpless.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道你的任务应该做什么，嗯，你会感到无助。

sentences.en: So we need, we need that structure.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要，我们需要这种结构。

sentences.en: We need those clarity of what is expected of us, but we also need to feel like we have some say in that, like we're not be, it's not being coercive, um, coerced.
sentences.zh: 我们需要明确对我们的期望是什么，但我们也需要觉得我们在其中有一些发言权，就像我们没有被，这不是强制性的，嗯，被强迫的。

sentences.en: We're not being coerced.
sentences.zh: 我们没有被强迫。

sentences.en: And so the best situation is whether, when, where there are these structures, but we also understand why they're there.
sentences.zh: 因此，最好的情况是存在这些结构，但我们也理解它们为什么存在。

sentences.en: We have reasons for them so that we can internalize their value.
sentences.zh: 我们有支持它们的理由，以便我们能够内化它们的价值。

sentences.en: And we have some opportunity to have input, some opportunity to respond to them if we think that they're not helping us.
sentences.zh: 并且我们有一些机会提出意见，如果我们认为它们对我们没有帮助，还有机会对它们做出反应。

sentences.en: And so, for example, corporations that have clear guidelines, but their employees also have some say in those guidelines and have an opportunity to, uh, give their opinions.
sentences.zh: 因此，例如，有明确准则的公司，但其员工对这些准则也有一定的发言权，并且有机会，呃，发表他们的意见。

sentences.en: That's what's really, you know, really, really, um, effective in a, in a workplace or in a, in a classroom, in a home.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正，你知道的，在工作场所、课堂或家庭中真正非常、非常，呃，有效的事情。

sentences.en: So, and we can think of this coming close to home for both Wendy and myself as, uh, and
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可以想到这对于温迪和我自己来说都离得很近，作为，呃，

sentences.en: Ben as well, I guess, as professors, right?
sentences.zh: 还有本，我想，作为教授，对吧？

sentences.en: Oftentimes we have students who come to us.
sentences.zh: 我们经常遇到学生来找我们。

sentences.en: They want to be researchers.
sentences.zh: 他们想成为研究人员。

sentences.en: If we just say to them, okay, decide on a topic you want to study and stuff, they are actually left hanging because they don't know how to proceed.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是对他们说，好吧，决定一个你想研究的主题之类的，他们其实会感到无所适从，因为他们不知道该如何进行。

sentences.en: But if we say, okay, this is the projects I'm working on.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们说，好吧，这是我正在做的项目。

sentences.en: We have a variety of questions here that you can choose from.
sentences.zh: 这里有各种各样的问题供你选择。

sentences.en: Then they can look, um, you've given them some structure within which to work.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可以看，嗯，你为他们提供了一些可以工作的框架。

sentences.en: They choose then which project they're going to work on.
sentences.zh: 然后他们选择要参与哪个项目。

sentences.en: And even as they progress through, they're doing the dissertation.
sentences.zh: 甚至随着他们的进展，他们在写毕业论文。

sentences.en: They have a committee, an advisor.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个委员会，一个导师。

sentences.en: Again, they are getting to make choices, but they get some structure around them to help guide them, you know, down the path.
sentences.zh: 同样，他们可以做出选择，但他们周围有一些结构来帮助指导他们，你知道的，沿着这条路走下去。

sentences.en: And without that structure, they'd be, even if they're successful, it would take a much longer time to get there.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这种结构，他们就会，即使他们成功了，到达终点也会花费更长的时间。

sentences.en: So last question, the final chapter of your book is about structural inequality and how the inequities in our society affect motivation for individuals.
sentences.zh: 所以最后一个问题，你们书的最后一章是关于结构性不平等以及我们社会中的不平等如何影响个人的动机。

sentences.en: Can, can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 能，能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: That of course is, um, I think, uh, uh, a myth that was really, really important for me.
sentences.zh: 这当然是，嗯，我认为，呃，对我来说非常非常重要的一个迷思。

sentences.en: Um, and I, I think for all of us, because again, this idea of motivation being a trait or individual,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为对我们所有人都很重要，因为同样，这种将动机视为一种特质或个人的观点，

sentences.en: we tend to focus on the individual who's unmotivated and we don't look at the context in which those individuals are.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于关注缺乏动机的个人，而没有看到这些个人所处的情境。

sentences.en: Um, and so take the example, I think one of the examples we used in the book was the wage gap, the gender wage gap.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就拿这个例子来说，我想我们在书中使用的例子之一就是薪酬差距，性别薪酬差距。

sentences.en: You know, so two people start working at a firm, um, and, and, you know, one is male, one is female, equal qualifications.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，两个人开始在一家公司工作，嗯，并且，你知道的，一个是男性，一个是女性，资质相同。

sentences.en: And then the female finds out that she's being paid, uh, you know, 80% of the salary that the male is being paid, although she's doing the same work, same level, right?
sentences.zh: 然后这位女性发现自己的薪水是，呃，你知道的，男性薪水的80%，尽管她做着同样的工作，同样的级别，对吧？

sentences.en: So then she can think, whoa, uh, you know, my work, actually, she can start devaluing the quality of the work that she does.
sentences.zh: 所以她就会想，哇，呃，你知道的，我的工作，事实上，她可以开始贬低自己所做工作的质量。

sentences.en: Not, but I am, you know, I thought I was doing good work, but I'm not really, because if I were, this wouldn't be happening.
sentences.zh: 不是的，但我，你知道的，我以为我做的是好工作，但我其实并没有，因为如果我是的话，就不会发生这种事了。

sentences.en: And so that her motivation would decrease and it may appear, okay, she's unmotivated, but what's happening is that the context to set her up, where I, the context is telling her
sentences.zh: 因此她的动机就会下降，这可能看起来，好吧，她缺乏动机，但实际发生的是，情境让她陷入了困境，或者说情境在告诉她

sentences.en: that, oh, you are not as good as, as somebody else.
sentences.zh: 哦，你没有其他人那么优秀。

sentences.en: And we know, of course, that this applies not just to gender, it applies to ethnic racial groups.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道这不仅适用于性别，还适用于种族群体。

sentences.en: Um, it applies to sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它适用于性取向。

sentences.en: There are many sort of demographic groups within societies that are sometimes marginalized in, in certain ways, um, uh, you know, and so, so the, the student in the classroom and
sentences.zh: 社会中存在许多人口统计学群体，他们在某些方面有时会被边缘化，嗯，你知道的，所以，所以课堂上的学生，

sentences.en: often in, in, in, in these contexts then as well, sometimes these people are, are loners or singletons, so they don't have anybody else to even talk to, to, to, to, to get a sense
sentences.zh: 而且通常在这些情境中也是如此，有时这些人是独行者或单身者，所以他们甚至没有任何其他人可以交谈，以获得一种感觉，即

sentences.en: of, um, is this normal?
sentences.zh: 这正常吗？

sentences.en: So, so that in fact, it really is incumbent upon teachers in the, in, in the classrooms that they set, how are you responding to the students when they put their hands up?
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上，这确实是教师在课堂上的责任，当学生举手时，你是如何回应的？

sentences.en: Do you have a way where in fact you are getting to every student and some students are not being left out unintentionally?
sentences.zh: 你有没有一种方法，事实上能够关注到每一个学生，而不会无意中漏掉某些学生？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not always intentional.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不总是故意的。

sentences.en: Um, if you are a, a, a, a, a supervisor in a company, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你是一家公司的，呃，呃，呃，呃，主管，对吧？

sentences.en: Are you giving feedback and clear directions to all of the, the employees again in the same way?
sentences.zh: 你是否同样以相同的方式向所有员工提供反馈和清晰的指导？

sentences.en: And do you have the employees help set up the structures that in fact allow for the feedback?
sentences.zh: 你是否让员工帮助建立实际上允许提供反馈的结构？

sentences.en: We come back to those things about autonomy, uh, competence and belonging, because that's the other thing that structural inequities do.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了关于自主性、呃、胜任感和归属感的事情上，因为这就是结构性不平等造成的另一件事。

sentences.en: They decrease belonging, right?
sentences.zh: 它们降低了归属感，对吧？

sentences.en: Do I really fit here?
sentences.zh: 我真的适合这里吗？

sentences.en: Uh, and stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so, so the structural inequities can affect all three of those major aspects of self-determination theory.
sentences.zh: 所以，结构性不平等会影响自我决定论的这三个主要方面。
